data.title: Dangote Refinery IPO is here: here’s what you need to know
data.description:
The Dangote Refinery IPO has kicked off, with millions of Nigerian investors rushing to buy the stock ahead of its eventual listing in October. Consequently, Aliko Dangote’s net worth is expected to cross the $50 billion milestone. 

Dangote Refinery IPO kicks off

Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, has kicked off the listing process of his giant refinery in Nigeria that seeks to raise $2.1 billion. This makes it the biggest IPO in Africa, and a major milestone for a company that has relied mostly on domestic funding. 

Millions of Nigerians have rushed to buy the stock, with some of the fastest growing brokers, including Bamboo, reporting outages. That’s because the so-called “peoples’ IPO” is highly affordable, with shares starting at 40 US cents, with the minimum investment being $4.

Dangote aims to raise $2.1 billion in this IPO, which will value the company at over $50 billion. According to Bloomberg, his net worth will jump to nearly $60 billion, catapulting him to the top 30 of the richest people in the world. He will become wealthier than people like Ken Griffin, Eric Schmidt, Masayoshi Son, and Abigail Johnson.

The fundraising process comes two months after the company raised $2 billion in a private placement that valued it at $39.1 billion. Femi Otodola, a Nigerian billionaire, invested $100 million at this time. As a result, there are concerns that retail investors are getting the raw end of the deal. 

A key risk that Nigerian investors face is that stocks often retreat immediately after their IPO. A good example of this is MTN Nigeria, whose stock initially rose to 108.6 naira shortly after the IPO and then crashed to 63 naira shortlyb after that. Since then, it has rebounded to 811 naira today. 

Most recently, SpaceX stock initially rose to $225 after its IPO and then crashed to a low of $105 after the listing. It remains substantially below its all-time high today. Similarly, Circle stock rose to $300 after the IPO and then dropped to the current $97. 

Dangote plans Kenyan refinery

The IPO comes at an interesting time for the company. It has already hit its 700k barrels a day output, making it the biggest refinery in Africa. This means that it has made Nigeria a net exporter of refined petroleum, which has helped to boost the Nigerian naira. Data shows that the USD/NGN dropped to 1,317, its lowest level since April 2024. It has slumped by over 24% from its highest point in 2025. 

Dangote Refinery plans to boost its investments in the coming months. It is about to start constructing a refinery project in Lamu, with the complex expected to be completed in the next three years. In addition to this, the company plans to build a 2,650 kilometer pipeline that runs from Namibia through Botswana to South Africa. In total, Dangote expects the refinery business to hit $100 billion in revenue in the next decade.

On top of this, Dangote has said that he plans to take other parts of his business empire public in the coming years.

The post Dangote Refinery IPO is here: here’s what you need to know appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Could a Fed hike push gold below $4,300 despite rising geopolitical risk?
data.description:
Gold steadied near $4,300 an ounce on Tuesday after sliding to its lowest level in more than a month, as investors balanced rising geopolitical risk against a stronger dollar and a sharp repricing of US interest rates ahead of the Federal Reserve’s policy decision.

Bullion recovered from Monday’s lows but remained under pressure after September futures settled at $4,310, their weakest close since August 6.

The move came as the 10-year US Treasury yield briefly crossed 5% for the first time since 2023, raising the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold.

Fed risk is dominating the gold trade

The immediate problem for gold is that the usual safe-haven playbook is not working cleanly.

Middle East tensions are worsening, but investors are also buying dollars and demanding higher bond yields as crude oil above $100 revives inflation concerns.

Markets are pricing a greater than 90% chance of a quarter-point Fed increase on Wednesday.

The September 15-16 meeting will also bring updated economic projections, leaving the new dot plot and Chair Kevin Warsh’s guidance at least as important for bullion as the rate decision itself.

Trade Nation senior market analyst David Morrison said that the recent price action suggests investors have increasingly favoured the dollar over gold as the immediate haven during periods of market stress.

That matters because a stronger greenback makes bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies.

Oil makes the Middle East risk more complicated

Gold would normally benefit from another escalation in the Middle East. This time, the transmission mechanism is less straightforward.

Brent crude has remained above $100 after attacks on Saudi infrastructure and worsening fighting around Yemen increased concern about regional supply routes.

Saudi Arabia’s damaged East-West pipeline has recently carried between 2.6 million and 4 million barrels a day and could remain constrained for several weeks.

Higher oil supports demand for geopolitical hedges, but it also raises the risk that US inflation remains sticky.

That keeps pressure on bonds and strengthens the case for tighter Fed policy, both of which work against gold.

BofA rates strategist Meghan Swiber told MarketWatch that once markets heavily price a rate increase, holding rates unchanged becomes harder because it risks another sharp rise in longer-term Treasury yields.

For gold, that means Wednesday’s decision is also a test of Fed credibility.

Gold rebound still needs confirmation

The technical picture reflects the same uncertainty. Gold is trying to stabilise around the psychologically important $4,300 level and remains close to its 50-day moving average near $4,275.

A sustained move above roughly $4,323 would improve the near-term tone and put the $4,400-$4,412 region back into focus.

However, failure to hold $4,275 would expose support around $4,234 and increase the risk of a deeper correction.

data.title: Why calls to slow AI may actually be good news for ServiceNow stock
data.description:
ServiceNow stock (NYSE: NOW) surged 7.4% on Monday as investors reconsidered one of the software sector’s biggest fears: that artificial intelligence agents will make established enterprise applications less valuable.

The stock closed at $142.35 on September 14, while the PHLX Semiconductor Index sank 5.9% after AI executives called for slower development of advanced models.

The contrast suggested investors were questioning which parts of the technology stack benefit if companies become more cautious about deploying powerful systems.

For ServiceNow, that debate cuts both ways, as slower development could reduce disruption risk while making AI governance more valuable.

The AI trade is shifting towards control

During the AI boom, semiconductor companies captured investor enthusiasm as hyperscalers poured money into computing infrastructure.

Software companies faced the opposite question: what happens if autonomous agents replace applications?

Monday’s session challenged that assumption. ServiceNow rallied as chipmakers fell, while enterprise software names also strengthened.

The shift had already been developing.

Morgan Stanley strategists led by Mike Wilson described the market as moving away from an “early-cycle, capital-intensive trade” towards businesses with strong free cash flow, AI adoption and asset-light models.

ServiceNow fits that profile, as unlike chipmakers or hyperscalers, it does not need to fund enormous data centres to participate in AI spending.

Its opportunity lies in the software layer through which companies manage AI.

Governance could become a bigger business

The stronger argument for ServiceNow is not merely that slower AI protects incumbent software. Widespread use of autonomous agents creates new problems around permissions, data access, security and accountability.

Needham analyst Mike Cikos raised his ServiceNow price target to $155 from $115 last week and maintained a Buy rating.

TipRanks reported that Needham came away from discussions with the company “incrementally more positive” on its positioning and roadmap, particularly around AI governance.

ServiceNow has been building directly into that problem. Its AI Control Tower helps companies discover, govern and monitor AI systems.

AI Gateway, now generally available within AI Control Tower, adds runtime controls over connections between agents and tools.

ServiceNow says it can enforce authentication and access policies, block sensitive responses, scan suspicious tools and pause servers or tools without code changes.

That matters if enterprises keep deploying agents but become less willing to let them operate without oversight. In that scenario, caution strengthens the case for the control layer ServiceNow wants to sell.

ServiceNow still needs the AI boom

There is an important contradiction. ServiceNow may benefit from greater concern about AI governance, but it still needs customers to adopt AI aggressively enough to support growth targets.

Bernstein, which reiterated an Outperform rating and a $248 price target, examined ServiceNow’s goal of $30 billion to $32 billion in annual contract value by 2030, with about 30% expected from AI.

According to Investing.com, analyst Peter Weed noted that reaching more than $9 billion of AI-derived ACV would require more than upgrades to AI-enabled products.

Consumption-based AI would also need to become material, raising questions about whether the target “seems like a stretch.”

That is the risk behind Monday’s rally. A slower race towards more autonomous models may ease fears that SaaS platforms will be rapidly displaced.

However, an outright slowdown in enterprise AI adoption would undermine ServiceNow’s own revenue opportunity.

The best outcome for ServiceNow is not an AI retreat, but continued enterprise adoption with tighter controls.

The post Why calls to slow AI may actually be good news for ServiceNow stock appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Why Wedbush and BofA issued bullish notes on Roblox stock today
data.description:
Roblox (RBLX) stock is ripping higher on September 14th on the back of bullish analyst notes and optimism around platform algorithm tweaks following developments at the recent RDC conference.

As investors cheered RBLX, it rallied past its 100-day moving average (MA) today, indicating the bullish momentum could actually sustain in the near-term.

The bullish Wall Street reports bring a much-needed reprieve to RBLX shares, which have tanked roughly 35% versus the start of this year (2026).

Wedbush and BofA raise price targets for Roblox stock

Analysts at both Wedbush and Bank of America Securities raised their price targets on RBLX stock to $48 this morning – pointing to management’s refined content discovery philosophy unveiled at RDC 2026.

According to them, the firm’s search and recommendation algorithm updates – which previously choked growth for viral experiences – are being adjusted to better personalize content delivery.

The surge in popularity of games like “Steal an Egg” serves as evidence that discovery velocity is recovering, they added.

Following the year-to-date decline, RBLX shares are trading at a price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of about 6x – which Wedbush and BofA analysts dubbed a significant discount to their historical valuation multiples.

That said, Roblox does not currently pay a dividend to attract income-focused investors as well.

Q3 bookings strength to drive RBLX shares higher

Wall Street analysts issued a bullish note on Roblox shares today also due to the expected upside in Q3 bookings.

Third-party platform tracking data (including metrics from RoMonitor) indicates that average peak concurrent users and engagement hours have rebounded strongly after July’s post-earnings drop.

This resurgence suggests that developer activity and player monetization are re-accelerating ahead of the crucial holiday quarter.

With daily active users (DAUs) stabilizing and international adoption picking up pace, institutional investors are growing increasingly confident that the company can outpace conservative consensus estimates when it reports third-quarter financial results.

Why has Roblox pushed higher in recent weeks?

Note that this latest upward move builds on a robust multi-week rally as Roblox continues to climb out of its multi-month lows following a brutal late-July post-earnings sell-off.

Heavy short covering has played a key role in squeezing the stock higher as sellers rush to exit bearish positions amid improving market sentiment.

Further underpinning this technical recovery is the strong structural support provided by the firm’s massive $3 billion share buyback authorization.

This capital return plan not only signals strong executive confidence in RBLX shares’ long-term enterprise value, but also provides continuous buying pressure that has effectively put a floor under the stock and sustained its upward momentum.

What’s the consensus rating on RBLX?

Investors should note that Wedbush and BofA remain among the more conservative Wall Street firms on Roblox.

The consensus rating on RBLX sits at Overweight, according to The Wall Street Journal, with price targets going as high as $65, indicating potential upside of another 30% from here.

data.title: Why is Oracle stock falling 4% today?
data.description:
Oracle shares ORCL fell 4.2% on Monday after co-founder Larry Ellison reversed plans to sell as much as $7.5 billion of his stake, while the company faces rising debt and another round of layoffs linked to its artificial intelligence infrastructure spending.

Oracle said Saturday that Ellison had abandoned the planned sale, one day after the company disclosed his trading plans.

The company said, “No Oracle stock was sold under that plan, and he has no other plans to sell any of his Oracle stock.”

The development came after a Friday securities filing revealed that Ellison had adopted a plan on June 22 to sell as many as 50 million Oracle shares, valued at roughly $7.5 billion based on recent prices.

The filing said the sales were expected to be completed by Oct. 24.

Ellison reverses planned Oracle share sale

Ellison has maintained a substantial stake in Oracle since the 1970s and remains one of the company's largest shareholders.

However, much of his wealth is tied to the stock.

A Wall Street Journal analysis found that about 24% of Ellison's roughly $200 billion net worth had been pledged as collateral.

He has also pledged more than $40 billion to support his son David Ellison's hostile bid for Warner Bros. in a deal valued at nearly $80 billion.

Ellison previously sold nearly $900 million of Oracle stock in January 2001, shortly before the company's shares fell almost 22% following lower-than-expected earnings.

He later agreed to pay $100 million to charity to settle an insider-trading lawsuit brought by shareholders.

Oracle ramps up AI spending and debt

Oracle is simultaneously pursuing an aggressive expansion of its AI infrastructure business.

The company plans to raise as much as $50 billion this year through stock and debt sales to finance data centres designed to handle expected growth in artificial intelligence computing.

Morgan Stanley credit analysts expect Oracle will require at least another $100 billion in financing during 2027 and the first half of 2028.

The company's rising debt burden has contributed to pressure on its shares this year.

Oracle stock has fallen more than 23% in 2026, while the technology-heavy Nasdaq has gained more than 13%.

Oracle reported $28.5 billion in first-quarter capital expenditures, up sharply from $8.5 billion a year earlier.

It also maintained its fiscal 2027 capital expenditure forecast at between $90 billion and $95 billion.

Layoffs add to pressure on Oracle

Oracle has also started another round of layoffs, said a Business insider report citing people affected by the cuts and an email reviewed by the publication.

The company told affected employees that their positions were being eliminated as part of a broader organisational change.

Oracle's workforce had already declined by 21,000 employees, or 13%, during the fiscal year ended May 31, according to a recent filing.

Oracle had around 141,000 employees before the latest round of cuts.

The layoffs come as the company continues to spend heavily on AI infrastructure.

While Wall Street remains uncertain about whether those investments will generate sufficient returns, Oracle's latest earnings report showed some positive developments, including cloud growth.

The post Why is Oracle stock falling 4% today? appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Why the BoE may stop selling long gilts as Britain’s bond stress deepens
data.description:
The Bank of England may stop selling some of its longest-dated government bonds as policymakers rethink quantitative tightening after a renewed surge in UK borrowing costs.

The Telegraph reported on Tuesday that the central bank is preparing to stop sales of 20- and 30-year gilts, with an announcement expected alongside Thursday’s monetary policy decision.

The move would deepen a shift already under way, rather than mark a sudden reversal of the Bank’s balance-sheet strategy.

The BoE has already scheduled no sales of gilts with maturities beyond 20 years during the current quarter, after progressively reducing its exposure to that part of the market.

Its gilt portfolio is expected to fall to about £488 billion by the end of September, from a peak of £895 billion in 2022.

Long gilts have become the pressure point

The rethink comes after an unusually painful period for long-dated UK debt.

Britain sold £4.25 billion of 30-year gilts last week at a yield of 5.8168%, the highest borrowing cost on such a syndicated sale since the Debt Management Office was created in 1998.

Thirty-year market yields have also approached 6% during the latest global bond sell-off.

Demand has not disappeared, the latest sale attracted more than £87 billion of orders, but the investor base has changed.

Defined-benefit pension schemes, once natural buyers of long gilts, have reduced their appetite as their liabilities mature.

Fund managers at Allianz Global Investors and RBC BlueBay told the Financial Times earlier this year that continued long-dated sales were becoming harder to justify as structural demand weakened.

Has quantitative tightening gone too far?

That is harder to answer than the recent sell-off suggests.

The BoE estimates that cumulative QT has added roughly 20 to 30 basis points to 10-year gilt yields since the programme began.

Its own analysis still describes the effect as modest relative to the much larger rise caused by changing rate expectations, global bond supply and higher term premiums.

Other estimates are less benign. Financial Times analysis has highlighted research suggesting QT may have increased UK borrowing costs by as much as 0.7 percentage points.

University of Liverpool professor Costas Milas argued that continuing aggressive QT while global yields are already climbing would be increasingly difficult to defend.

Slower QT would not mean easier monetary policy

Stopping long-gilt sales would therefore be better viewed as a change in implementation than a pivot towards monetary easing.

Markets expect the BoE to slow the overall pace of balance-sheet reduction, potentially to around £50 billion over the next year from £70 billion currently.

Bank Rate, meanwhile, remains the central tool for controlling inflation.

That distinction matters with oil above $100 and UK inflation risks rising again.

The BoE could keep policy restrictive through interest rates while avoiding unnecessary pressure on the weakest part of the gilt curve.

If Thursday confirms that approach, the message may be that quantitative tightening itself has not gone too far, but selling long gilts into a structurally thinner market perhaps has.

The post Why the BoE may stop selling long gilts as Britain’s bond stress deepens appeared first on Invezz

data.title: HPE stock declines 8% on Monday: here's why
data.description:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) shares fell 8% on Monday after Evercore ISI downgraded the stock to In Line from Outperform, citing its sharp recent rally and more balanced risk-reward profile.

The brokerage maintained its $65 price target.

HPE shares closed at $62.08 on Friday, Sept. 11, after gaining 15% over the previous five trading sessions and 184% over the past six months.

According to Evercore analyst Amit Daryanani, the stock had risen 158.5% year to date, compared with an 11.9% gain for the S&P 500.

HPE was also up 37.6% in the third quarter, while the benchmark index had gained 2.1%.

Evercore says HPE shares are fairly valued

Daryanani said the downgrade reflected the recent appreciation in HPE’s share price.

The stock was trading at 13 times projected fiscal 2027 earnings, compared with its five-year average of eight times.

“Given the stock now trading at 13x FY27 P/E versus its five-year average of 8x and 14x EV/’27 FCF, in line with its historical average, we believe shares are fairly valued at current levels,” Daryanani wrote in a note to clients.

Evercore said the company’s recent re-rating was supported by fundamental improvements.

The brokerage credited HPE management with strong execution during the first year of integrating Juniper Networks, particularly amid challenging supply conditions.

HPE shares have gained 192% since the Juniper acquisition closed, according to Evercore.

However, the firm said the setup could become more difficult from this point, with fewer immediate catalysts available to support another expansion in the stock’s valuation multiple.

Juniper integration and networking margins remain key

Evercore identified three developments that could make it more constructive on HPE shares.

The first is continued progress in integrating Juniper Networks, particularly if the integration leads to higher margins.

The second involves the company’s business mix and margin quality.

Evercore noted that cloud and artificial intelligence activities generate lower margins than networking equipment.

The third potential catalyst is any benefit from HPE’s Helios opportunity.

The brokerage expects those potential tailwinds to emerge primarily during fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028.

Networking remains particularly important to HPE’s profitability, accounting for more than half of segment operating profit.

Although networking orders increased 36% in the July quarter, pro forma revenue rose 10%, trailing the growth reported by Cisco and Arista, according to Evercore.

HPE faces a tougher setup after strong rally

Evercore said HPE’s recent performance had been justified by improvements in execution and the Juniper integration.

Nevertheless, the firm believes further gains could depend on stronger networking supply conditions and additional margin improvement.

“From here, however, we see a tougher setup,” Daryanani wrote, adding that the balance between potential returns and risks had become more even.

“With risk/reward more balanced at current levels, we are moving to the sidelines with an In Line rating,” he said.

The post HPE stock declines 8% on Monday: here's why appeared first on Invezz

data.title: Netflix stock rises as Evercore raises price target to $110
data.description:
Netflix shares NFLX rose about 4.3% on Monday after Evercore ISI increased its price target on the streaming company to $110 from $100 and reiterated its Outperform rating.

The new target implies roughly 42% upside from Netflix’s previous closing price.

The brokerage cited improving subscriber trends in the United States and Japan, as well as growth opportunities from live events, short-form content and advertising.

Netflix penetration reaches multi-year high in US

Evercore analyst Kutgun Maral said Netflix’s penetration rate reached a multi-year high of 63% in the US.

In Japan, penetration rose to a record 22%, according to the brokerage’s surveys.

Churn intentions also improved in both markets, although customer satisfaction remained a concern in the US.

The findings came from Evercore ISI’s 58th quarterly US subscriber survey and its semi-annual survey in Japan.

The brokerage said the results strengthened its view that Netflix retains strong subscriber engagement and pricing power.

Netflix stock climbed 4.32% in morning trading to $80.74.

The valuation framework was extended to 2028, using 25 times the firm’s 2028 earnings-per-share estimate.

Citi also maintained a Buy rating and a $100 price target in a recent note.

Live events and short-form content offer growth opportunities

Evercore identified live programming as a potential driver of subscriber growth and engagement.

In Japan, 45% of newly surveyed subscribers said they joined Netflix as part of the company’s World Baseball Classic promotion.

The survey also showed that the percentage of users who had watched live events increased to 60% in September from 42% in March.

The brokerage also highlighted Netflix Clips, the company’s short-form video feed.

Around 46% of Japanese respondents and 38% of US respondents said they had scrolled through the feature.

Evercore said live events and short-form videos could support engagement and retention.

The company’s advertising-supported tier was also attracting new and returning subscribers.

Netflix’s margins and buybacks support earnings growth

Netflix’s broader strategy remains focused on growing revenue and operating profit while managing content costs.

Management is targeting an operating margin of 31.5% this year, up from 29.5% last year and 26.5% two years ago.

Content costs increased 11.5% in the first half of 2026, while total viewing hours rose 2% year over year.

The company has also expanded its live programming and added lower-cost content, including video podcasts.

The advertising business is expected to generate approximately $3 billion this year.

A Motley Fool report said advertising could provide further growth through increased ad-supported viewing, new products and improvements to Netflix’s advertising technology.

Netflix also repurchased a record $4.7 billion of its shares in the second quarter. Its board had authorised an additional $25 billion in buybacks, with $27.1 billion remaining under existing authorisations at the end of June.

Evercore described Netflix as a sustainable 20% earnings-per-share growth company, although it expects the company’s catalyst path to become more visible in 2027 rather than 2026.

The post Netflix stock rises as Evercore raises price target to $110 appeared first on Invezz

data.title: AI panic triggers a rally in CrowdStrike stock
data.description:
CrowdStrike (CRWD) stock is ripping higher on Monday morning, defying a broader tech rout, to hit an all-time intraday high of $238.68.

Investors are aggressively bidding up pure-play security firms today following heightened urgency around AI vulnerabilities, propelling CRWD far past the broader software index.

Including today’s gains, CrowdStrike shares are up more than 100% versus the start of this year.

What’s driving CrowdStrike stock higher today?

Urgent safety warnings issued over the weekend by executives across leading artificial intelligence frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI sparked a wave of enterprise fear.

Industry leaders cautioned that rapidly evolving autonomous agents and machine-speed AI workflows are expanding the corporate attack surface much faster than traditional IT teams can manage.

Rather than dampening sentiment, the threat profile drove huge sums of institutional capital into specialized cybersecurity firms tasked with securing next-generation software infrastructure.

CRWD stock emerged as a key beneficiary as investors wagered that complex artificial intelligence deployment directly expands mission-critical security spending.

What else is helping CRWD shares rally?

CrowdStrike stock is rallying today also because, as macro uncertainties weighed on semiconductor manufacturers and hardware suppliers, traders executed a notable capital rotation out of hardware and into high-margin software operators.

Software pure-plays equipped with recurring subscription revenues saw immediate inflows – with CrowdStrike, Zscaler, and Palo Alto Networks leading the charge.

Institutional funds are seeking shelter in platform security names whose growth trajectories remain insulated from supply chain friction, hardware cycles, or chip export constraints, making enterprise cybersecurity a top defensible AI trade.

Fal.Con momentum remains a tailwind

Finally, CRWD shares printed a new high as market momentum continues to build on the heels of the recent Fal.Con 2026 annual conference, where executive leadership unveiled Falcon Guardian and SafeMind.

These specialized tools are designed specifically to monitor, audit, and protect autonomous agents operating within corporate cloud networks.

Along with ambitious long-term financial targets including reaching $10 billion in annual recurring revenue (ARR) by the end of this decade and double it again by fiscal 2035, CrowdStrike Holdings looks like an increasingly attractive long-term bet.

How Wall Street recommends playing CrowdStrike

CrowdStrike’s breakout rally underscores a structural shift in enterprise technology: security is no longer an afterthought, but the primary enabler of scale.

By directly addressing the threat profile of autonomous AI agents – while capturing “hardware-to-software” capital flows, CRWD has cemented its market dominance.

As management delivers on its longer-term revenue goals, CRWD stands exceptionally positioned to command the AI-driven cybersecurity era.

Investors should also note that despite massive year-to-date outperformance, Wall Street analysts remain bullish as ever on CrowdStrike for the next 12 months.

According to Barchart, the consensus rating on the cybersecurity giant sits at Moderate Buy, with price targets going as high as $425, indicating potential for another 75% rally from here.

data.title: Nvidia stock: Should investors buy the dip amid AI slowdown fears?
data.description:
Nvidia stock NVDA fell nearly 3% on Monday as concerns over the pace of artificial intelligence development triggered a selloff in AI-related equities.

The decline came after executives at major AI companies called for a slower approach to advancing increasingly capable models.

The broader market also weakened, with the S&P 500 falling 0.33%, the Nasdaq Composite declining 0.38% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average losing 0.12%.

The selloff has raised questions over whether investors should buy the dip in Nvidia, wait for further clarity or reduce their exposure to the chipmaker.

AI slowdown concerns weigh on Nvidia stock

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for AI companies to slow the rate at which they advance model capabilities in a lengthy essay published on X on Saturday.

He cited growing concerns about the potential misuse of artificial intelligence.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI chief Elon Musk said they agreed with Amodei's proposal.

Altman also said OpenAI would not proceed with an initial public offering this year, citing safety concerns.

The comments have prompted investors to reassess the rapid expansion of AI development and the substantial spending that has supported demand for advanced computing infrastructure.

A slower pace of AI development could potentially reduce the need for heavy investment in the technology.

That would create a risk for chipmakers such as Nvidia, whose business has benefited from the expansion of AI infrastructure.

Bernstein analysts led by Stacy Rasgon said the developments could further depress sentiment across the semiconductor sector, which had already been recovering after falling roughly 19% from its June peak.

Bernstein says buy weakness in Nvidia

Despite the recent pressure, Bernstein reiterated its Outperform ratings on Nvidia and Broadcom and recommended buying weakness in both stocks.

The analysts argued that a slowdown in the pace of AI development does not necessarily mean a slowdown in spending.

They noted that Amodei had not called for a halt to AI training, but rather a shift from an extremely fast pace to a somewhat slower one.

Bernstein said such a pace could still represent significant growth for the industry. The firm also pointed to rising demand from AI inference and agentic applications.

The analysts noted that there is already insufficient computing capacity to meet demand for even existing AI models, suggesting that infrastructure requirements could remain substantial despite concerns over the pace of model development.

Anthropic's own spending also provides context for the debate.

According to The Information, the company agreed to 14.8 gigawatts of computing capacity involving approximately $517 billion in commitments over the 11 months through August.

The Financial Times also reported that Anthropic expects a second consecutive quarter of adjusted operating profit, with inference gross margins exceeding 80% before distribution costs.

Nvidia's broader AI strategy offers support

Nvidia has been seeking to reduce its dependence on a small number of major customers by supporting a wider AI ecosystem.

The company has invested in startups and backed open-source AI models, which users can download and modify.

Earlier this month, Nvidia agreed to acquire open-source AI development platform Hugging Face in a $12.9 billion deal, according to the report.

The chipmaker also has customers whose AI ambitions may continue regardless of calls for slower development.

Musk, for example, has said SpaceX is highly confident it will launch Nvidia-powered AI servers in space next year.

SpaceX has previously indicated that it plans to use Nvidia hardware for orbital data centres, potentially addressing some of the land and power constraints facing conventional facilities.

However, the economic viability of orbital data centres remains subject to skepticism.

The post Nvidia stock: Should investors buy the dip amid AI slowdown fears? appeared first on Invezz
